name: bb_squeeze_breakout_5s
author: adapted from quant_system
thesis: When Bollinger Band width compresses to a multi-day low, volatility is coiling and a directional move is imminent. The squeeze resolves into a breakout as accumulated orders fire. The inefficiency exists because many participants interpret tight Bollingers as 'no opportunity' and leave the screen, reducing competition at the moment of breakout. Not fully arbitraged because the direction of the breakout is unknown — you must react, not predict.
mechanism: Bollinger band extremes indicate price has moved beyond 2 standard deviations from its recent mean. This typically results from a liquidity-driven overshoot rather than fundamental revaluation. Market makers and statistical arbitrageurs recognize the overshoot and trade against it, while the original directional flow exhausts, creating a natural mean-reversion within 30-90 seconds.

exit.signal_exit: exit if close re-enters inside bands and bb_width starts expanding

weaknesses: Squeeze detection on 1-min bars with 20-bar lookback captures 20-minute squeezes — these are much noisier than daily squeezes. Many false squeezes.
The breakout direction from a squeeze is random — you're betting on follow-through, not prediction. Win rate is ~42% and losses are common.
Bollinger Bands are the most widely-known retail indicator. Any edge from BB analysis is heavily competed away.
prior_art: Bollinger Band Squeeze. John Bollinger's original work. See also: TTM Squeeze (John Carter) for Keltner channel variant.
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; apply to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index instead of FnO universe; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
